item.title: Is a Matched-Pairs t-Test Appropriate? Headphones and Focus Scores
item.stimulus: A counselor suspects that noise-cancelling headphones improve students' focus scores. She randomly selected 14 students from a large college. Each student took a focus test once with headphones and once without, in a random order, and the counselor recorded each student's difference (score without headphones minus score with headphones) in points. The sample of 14 differences has mean −6.4 points and standard deviation 9.8 points. A dotplot of the 14 differences is strongly skewed with one outlier.

parts.prompt: Define the parameter of interest and state the null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

criteria.text: Defines μ_d as the μ_d is the true mean difference (focus score without headphones minus focus score with headphones), in points, for all students at this college.
criteria.evidence: Response defines μ_d as the μ_d is the true mean difference (focus score without headphones minus focus score with headphones), in points, for all students at this college, naming the response variable and the population in context.
criteria.fix: Name the parameter with its symbol and say which population mean (or mean difference) it is, in context.

criteria.text: States H₀: μ_d = 0 and Hₐ: μ_d < 0.
criteria.evidence: Response writes H₀: μ_d = 0 and Hₐ: μ_d < 0, with the alternative in the correct direction.
criteria.fix: Write the null with an equals sign and take the direction of the alternative from the question being investigated.

parts.prompt: For the appropriate procedure, decide whether its conditions are met. Justify each decision.

criteria.text: Checks the randomization condition: the 14 students were randomly selected.
criteria.evidence: Response states the randomization condition in context: the 14 students were randomly selected.
criteria.fix: Check that the data came from random selection or random assignment, and say how, in context.

criteria.text: Checks the 10% condition: 14 students are less than 10% of the students at the college.
criteria.evidence: Response checks that the sample size is less than 10% of the population: 14 students are less than 10% of the students at the college.
criteria.fix: When sampling without replacement, compare each sample size with 10% of its population to confirm independence.

criteria.text: Checks the sample-data condition: the sample of differences has n = 14, which is less than 30, and its dotplot is strongly skewed with one outlier, so the sample-data condition is not met and the t-test is not appropriate.
criteria.evidence: Response states the sample-data condition, says whether it is met, and gives the reason: the sample of differences has n = 14, which is less than 30, and its dotplot is strongly skewed with one outlier, so the sample-data condition is not met and the t-test is not appropriate.
criteria.fix: State the condition that applies: sample sizes of at least 30, or samples with no strong skewness or outliers.

parts.prompt: A classmate proposes a two-sample t-test that compares the mean focus score with headphones and the mean focus score without headphones for these students. Is that appropriate? Explain.

criteria.text: States that the classmate's two-sample t-test is not appropriate, because each student provided both scores, so the two sets of scores are not independent samples; the analysis should use the 14 differences (a matched-pairs, one-sample procedure).
criteria.evidence: Response rejects the classmate's two-sample t-test and gives the reason: each student provided both scores, so the two sets of scores are not independent samples; the analysis should use the 14 differences (a matched-pairs, one-sample procedure).
criteria.fix: Check whether the two measurements come from the same individuals; if so, analyze the differences with a one-sample procedure.

item.model_answer:
(a) Μ_d is the true mean difference (focus score without headphones minus focus score with headphones), in points, for all students at this college. H₀: μ_d = 0 versus Hₐ: μ_d < 0.

(b) The procedure is a one-sample t-test for a population mean difference (matched pairs), applied to the 14 differences. Randomization: the 14 students were randomly selected. 10% condition: 14 students are less than 10% of the students at the college. Sample-data condition: the sample of differences has n = 14, which is less than 30, and its dotplot is strongly skewed with one outlier, so the sample-data condition is not met and the t-test is not appropriate.

(c) No. Each student provided both scores, so the two sets of scores are not independent samples; the analysis should use the 14 differences (a matched-pairs, one-sample procedure).
